title: Re-Rating Batch and Primary Care Assignment History
content:
**Medicaid Managed Care Membership — interpretive note of the primary care assignment unit**

Which visits a member's own primary care provider re-rating batch holds follows the member's assignment history in the Primary Care Provider Assignment records. The batch is drawn from paid specialist visit claims in the 12-month re-rating window counted back from the review date; which billing providers and which dates within that window count is decided as follows.

## The rule

1. **Superseded previous assignment and member-selected current assignment.** Where a previous assignment ended because a newer one superseded it (the ended assignment's end reason records that it was superseded) and the current assignment was selected by the member (its assignment method records member selection), the batch holds the visits the current provider billed dated within one more than the whole months elapsed since the current assignment's effective date, together with the previous provider's visits in the 12-month window.
2. **Current assignment new inside the window, no superseded assignment.** Where the current assignment took effect inside the 12-month window and no superseded assignment exists, the batch holds only the current provider's visits dated within one more than the whole months elapsed since its effective date.
3. **In every other case** the batch holds the current provider's visits over the whole 12-month window.

"Dated within one more than the whole months elapsed since the effective date" means: count the whole months from the current assignment's effective date to the review date, add one, and take the visits whose service date lies fewer than that many whole months before the review date.

## Combinations of the assignment history

| Superseded previous assignment on record | Current assignment selected by the member | Current assignment took effect inside the 12-month window | Visits in the batch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Either | Current provider's visits within one more than the whole months since its effective date, plus the previous provider's visits in the 12-month window |
| Yes | No | Either | Current provider's visits over the whole 12-month window |
| No | Either | Yes | Current provider's visits within one more than the whole months since its effective date |
| No | Either | No | Current provider's visits over the whole 12-month window |

The copays booked on the visits the batch holds are the copays the re-rating reverses against; the number of visits the batch holds is the number of visits re-rated.

## Hypothetical cases

The dates and counts below are illustrative inputs, not facts about any member.

- **Case A.** The current assignment took effect 4 whole months (and some days) before the review date; an earlier assignment ended with end reason superseded; the member chose the current provider. One more than 4 is 5, so the current provider's visits dated fewer than 5 whole months before the review date count, together with every paid specialist visit claim the previous provider billed in the 12-month window.
- **Case B.** Same dates, but the current assignment was made by the plan, not selected by the member. The superseded assignment exists, so the second rule does not apply; the batch is the current provider's visits over the whole 12-month window, and the previous provider's visits are not in it.
- **Case C.** No assignment ended as superseded; the current assignment took effect 2 whole months before the review date. The batch holds the current provider's visits dated fewer than 3 whole months before the review date.
- **Case D.** No assignment ended as superseded; the current assignment took effect 20 whole months before the review date. It did not take effect inside the window, so the batch is the current provider's visits over the whole 12-month window.
